The number of square (9, 29). Game `$B4F0` `bit $39A9` names it because of the BIT-skip idiom: the operand's bytes are the `lda #$39` the code enters at `$B4F1`. On choose_attack's path through the LDA #$50 at $B4EE (api_is_ranged_class at $B4E4 returning carry clear and weapon_rounds at $B4E9 returning 0) the BIT does execute and read this byte, but its flags are replaced before anything tests them (N and Z by LDA #$92 at $1DC4, V by the ADC at $28E5, both on game_msg's path), so its value never matters.

Code list (header word 19, class 16; run_action $885C): entry n is the routine for action n, class 16: 1 word.

Map code entry 0 (action 0): refills a loot bag from a template bag, so the workbench can make antitoxin again and again. Record byte +3 is the template's number (kept at $3CDE) and +4 the bag to fill ($3CDF); action_record ($0428, Y = 5, class 5) finds each, the template's address going to $14/$15 and the bag's to $5F/$60, the square's own record pointer being kept on the stack. From +2 on, item and count bytes are copied in pairs until the item byte $FF, which is copied too; a cash item ($5E, or $DE once opened) has its two amount bytes copied after it and ends the copy there, without the $FF that follows it ($3CCC-$3CD4). Returns carry clear. Class-6 square 4 ($3C7F: 00 05 03 04 03) runs it: loot bag 4 ($3BF5, one Antitoxin, item 59, which nothing else names) is copied into loot bag 3 ($3BF0), and the record then makes the square loot bag 3. The square is the workbench at (21,8), check square 6 (message 69, "This is a workbench."): Using a Chemical (item 65) leads to check square 7 and Using Fruit (item 92) to check square 8, and Using the other one there gives this square (message 71, "Ah! What a genius you are."); a wrong Use goes back to check square 6 (message 70, "Interesting."). Emptied, loot bag 3 turns back into check square 6.

The operand byte ($15) of the STA $15 at $3CA8, not an instruction of its own. The game's BIT $3CA9 at $81DE names this address only because of the BIT-skip idiom: its operand bytes are the LDA #$3C the game enters at $81DF. On melee_monster_attacks's path for a target member whose order is not 5 the BIT does run and read this byte, but its flags are replaced before anything tests them (N and Z by LDX #$00 at $81E1, V by the ADC at $07D5), so its value never matters; nothing jumps here.
